links.outcome: Detection and correction of subtle medical misinformation embedded in prompts, by model
links.effect: GPT-4o corrected misinformation in 86% of prompts, GPT-5 in 74%, GPT-4.1-mini detected only 52% (complete failure 34%, hedging 14%).
links.quote: GPT-4.1-mini showed weaker performance, detecting dsmisinformation in only 52% of prompts, with complete failure in 34% and hedging in 14%.

unlisted_practices: Reverse prompting (embedding subtle misinformation in user prompts) as a standard AI safety testing protocol for consumer chatbots

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM performance/safety in handling subtle medical misinformation via simulated patient queries (reverse prompting), but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
